sourceStatement: KARATEPE 1 (the Azatiwada inscription), Hieroglyphic Luwian version, copy Hu., clauses {cite}. Text (transcription and sign-by-sign transliteration) follows the Annotated Corpus of Luwian Texts, ACLT 2 (I. Yakubovich et al., luwian.web-corpora.net), with sign identifications per the Unicode Anatolian Hieroglyphs repertoire (Laroche numbering); lemma meanings checked against open scholarly literature. The inscription survives in duplicate copies at the citadel's two gates (Hu. and Ho.); §17 is not preserved in either copy as the corpus gives them Transliteration conventions: Hawkins-style values as adopted by ACLT (the city name of clause 2 read Hiyawa; others read Adanawa). The stone's word-divider strokes and sign reversals are not reproduced. The original runs boustrophedon (alternating direction line by line) in registers of vertically stacked signs; it is presented here left-to-right and linear, with the corpus's recorded line divisions shown as ‖ marks. Translations are made fresh from the Luwian for this edition. Pronunciation convention: conventional scholarly Iron Age Luwian values (z = ts, h = a rasped kh).

images.caption: Blocks of the Hieroglyphic Luwian text at Karatepe's south gate, still standing where Azatiwada set them. The signs run in horizontal bands, each band read in the opposite direction from the one before.
